source.title: Implicit regularization of deep residual networks towards neural ODEs
source.authors: P. Marion; Yu-Han Wu; M. E. Sander; Gérard Biau

record.tranche_reason: Reports train and test accuracy for CIFAR-10 residual networks under different activation and initialization conditions, but does not test a listed claim version directly.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 accuracy results bear on natural-label train/test performance. The study does not test random-label memorization, width past interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected networks, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Cited prior-work results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests preservation of a neural ODE structure during residual-network training. Its CIFAR-10 activation and initialization comparisons do not test V1–V8. Synthetic experiments fit independent Gaussian targets but report only optimization and weight smoothness, without the held-out and natural-label comparisons required by V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors prove a large-depth neural ODE limit for suitably scaled, smoothly initialized residual networks under finite-horizon clipped gradient flow, and a joint infinite-time/infinite-depth limit under additional local PL and target-size assumptions. Their CIFAR-10 experiments illustrate preservation of smooth weights with Identity or GELU and weight-tied initialization. They describe a performance cost relative to i.i.d. initialization, most clearly demonstrated by GELU.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient flow for theoretical results and a convolutional CIFAR-10 experiment with SGD; studies convergence toward neural ODEs rather than the listed generalization interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported CIFAR-10 train/test accuracies vary with activation function and initialization scheme. The authors also report that weight-tied initialization preserves smooth weights for Identity and GELU but not ReLU, while i.i.d. initialization does not preserve smoothness.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, weight-tied versus i.i.d. initialization gives test accuracy of 79.9% versus 85.7% with GELU, 59.8% versus 59.6% with Identity, and 88.1% versus 88.4% with ReLU. Only weight-tied Identity and GELU preserve smooth trained weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation and initialization affect accuracy and preservation of a neural ODE structure in these convolutional residual networks; the initialization-related accuracy penalty is most apparent with GELU.

record.problems: The real-world experiment uses one dataset and a specialized residual architecture; smoothness is assessed by visual inspection. Results do not compare the claim's listed interventions or measures.

untested.parts: No matched random-label and natural-label training experiments with held-out accuracy.
No measurement of test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
No dropout or dropout-plus-weight-decay removal comparison.
No magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: All twelve accuracy values and their activation/initialization assignments match Table 1. Their states remain cannot_determine because none measures a listed claim's effect; this does not imply that the reported accuracies are unreadable. Smoothness across layers is distinct from loss-landscape sharpness in V7.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or compare random-label and natural-label generalization.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No comparison with fully connected networks or test of local connectivity.
Does not measure sharpness or compare it with generalization gaps.
Does not remove memorized training examples.
